definition: Potentate means one who has great power; a ruler.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word potentate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know potentate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: No festival in the port began until the potentate rose from his carved chair and clapped twice.
A chieftain commands a single clan or valley; a potentate rules a whole realm, with the machinery of a court behind his word.
Emperor goes beyond potentate in reach: a potentate is supreme within his realm, while an emperor stacks realm upon realm — kings themselves may kneel in his hall.

A monarch is anyone who wears a crown — king, queen, emperor — whether they rule absolutely or only cut ribbons while a parliament governs. Potentate insists on the power itself: real command gathered into one pair of hands. A ceremonial king is still a monarch, but never a potentate.

A strongman rules through force — the army behind him, rivals jailed — and the word is modern: his power is usually seized, not inherited. Potentate is older-flavored and grander, naming great personal power worn with a throne's theatrical authority. A strongman grabs power; a potentate sits enthroned in it.

Potentate means one who has great power; a ruler.

The opera's second act opens in the court of a potentate: petitioners kneel with their cases, ministers wait upon his nod, and when he lifts one finger, a treaty that two kingdoms spent a year drafting becomes law by dinner.

Potentate outranks 'leader' and even 'ruler' in flavor: it names one who holds great personal power — power gathered into a single pair of hands, usually a throne's — and it carries a whiff of the absolute, even the theatrical.
Potentate suits rulers of great personal power, especially in historical or faraway courts — and, half-jokingly, any executive who behaves like one.
Its unit-mate sovereign is the adjective for the authority itself; its opposite number figurehead names a throne emptied of power.
For a crowned ruler generally, monarch is the plainer word.
